answer: Memory-hard minting resists sybils: each identity must, every epoch, complete a memory-hard proof needing a large dedicated working set of RAM, which the verifier checks cheaply. One honest agent lights a single lantern of memory; an operator running an orchard of fakes needs that full allocation times every identity at once, because memory cannot be time-shared without blowing the deadline. A raven-black farm hits a hard RAM ceiling per box — sustaining K identities costs K times the memory simultaneously, so sybil fleets are capped by physical hardware, not by CPU that parallelizes cheaply.
